# Why start here

## The plan

Modal logic interprets $\Box$ and $\Diamond$ over a set of worlds with a binary relation.

. . .

Almost every later result turns on which **properties** that relation has.

::: {.notes}
Tell them explicitly: today looks like set theory, but every definition
reappears as an axiom in week 8.
:::

# Relations

## Ordered pairs

Ordered Pair

:   $\langle x, y \rangle$ is the ordered pair of $x$ and $y$.

. . .

Order matters:

$$
\langle x, y \rangle = \langle u, v \rangle \ \text{ iff } \ x = u \text{ and } y = v
$$

## Binary relations

Binary Relation

:   A binary relation $R$ on $W$ is a set of ordered pairs of members of $W$:
    $R \subseteq W \times W$.

. . .

We write $Rxy$ for $\langle x, y \rangle \in R$.

Read it as '$x$ sees $y$', or '$y$ is **accessible** from $x$'.

# Properties

## Reflexivity and symmetry

Reflexivity

:   $Rxx$ for every $x \in W$.

. . .

Symmetry

:   For all $x, y \in W$: if $Rxy$ then $Ryx$.

## Transitivity and seriality

Transitivity

:   For all $x, y, z \in W$: if $Rxy$ and $Ryz$, then $Rxz$.

. . .

Seriality

:   For every $x \in W$ there is some $y \in W$ with $Rxy$.

## Euclidean

Euclidean

:   For all $x, y, z \in W$: if $Rxy$ and $Rxz$, then $Ryz$.

. . .

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
Draw this one. It is the property students consistently cannot picture.
:::

# Independence

## A cautionary case {.smaller}

Symmetry and transitivity together do **not** give reflexivity.

Let $W = \{1, 2\}$ and $R = \{\langle 1, 1 \rangle\}$.

::: {.incremental}
- Symmetric? ✅ --- the only pair is $\langle 1,1 \rangle$
- Transitive? ✅ --- vacuously
- Reflexive? ❌ --- $2$ does not see itself
:::

::: {.notes}
Make them try to build this themselves before revealing it.
:::

# The payoff

## Frames validate axioms {.smaller}

A frame validates an axiom exactly when its relation has the matching property.

| Axiom | Schema | Property of $R$ |
|-------|--------|-----------------|
| D | $\Box \varphi \to \Diamond \varphi$ | serial |
| T | $\Box \varphi \to \varphi$ | reflexive |
| B | $\varphi \to \Box \Diamond \varphi$ | symmetric |
| 4 | $\Box \varphi \to \Box \Box \varphi$ | transitive |
| 5 | $\Diamond \varphi \to \Box \Diamond \varphi$ | euclidean |

. . .

This table is the spine of the completeness results.
